messages:
kai: Canary alert for reserved pool rsv-v2 in us-west-2. After today's rollout (merge 09b3f) the p95 jumped ~2x on heavy-seq traffic. Seeing timeouts from a few tenants. Anyone watching canary?

oliver: Yep, alerted by CI perf. The perf/batching CI matrix shows regressions only when the new kernel selector + prefetcher settings are enabled. Reproducer script failing locally.

sophia: Initial read: selector now biases fused-attn for sequences >1k even at batch=1. Fused-attn latency is worse for single-stream long sequences. Might be a heuristic tuning bug.

maria: Telemetry also shows a KV-cache eviction spike starting at the same commit window. Prefetch window shrink may be evicting more prefixes and increasing cold fills.

kai: Snippet from canary node-3 logs:
```
[2026-01-08T07:03:14Z] req=rc-7f
selected_kernel=fused_attn_v2
batch=1
seq_len=1792
kv_cache_hit=0.10
latency_p95_ms=378
```
That p95 is way above smoke threshold.

sophia: Short mitigation: flip kernel-selector to prefer baseline kernel for reserved pools and seq_len>=1024. We can flip via feature-ops without reverting the merge.

oliver: I'm bisecting the merge now. There are three topical changes in 09b3f: selector heuristic, prefetch window change, and an autobatching tweak. Alone each shows small delta; together they amplify.

dev-bot: deploybot: automated rollback hold triggered for rollout rsv-v2 (healthcheck p95 exceeded). Rollout paused.

anna: Oncall concurs. Opening incident and notifying CS. We'll mark the rollout on hold and start incident comms.

kai: Proposed decision path: 1) flip selector flag in canary immediately; 2) observe 10-20 minutes; 3a) if p95 returns to baseline, push hotpatch for selector and continue with prefetch tuning; 3b) if not, perform full revert of 09b3f.

maria: Important note: even if selector hotpatch helps latency, the eviction spike (+42% evictions in telemetry) increases backend load and tail variability. We need coordinated follow-up.

sophia: Running a 60s profile on node-3 after flag flip: `profiler --target node-3 --duration 60 --labels canary`. Will upload flamegraphs.

kai: Flag flipped at 07:12Z to canary nodes. Early metrics: p95 dropped ~25%, timeouts stopped. Holding off full rollout.

oliver: Bisect update: interaction pattern identified. Selector change increases probability of taking fused-attn on long sequences; prefetch shrink reduces KV reuse; combined they make the off-path expensive.

sophia: Kernel call counts from profiler (post-flag): fused_attn_v2 calls down ~80% in canary samples; baseline kernel calls up proportionally. Will attach flamegraphs in incident.

kai: Oncall-bot created incident #inc-3019: "reserved capacity canary p95 spike after merge 09b3f". Responders: anna, kai, oliver, sophia, maria.

anna: Sending customer-facing note template to CS. Asking accounts team to route any performance reports to #inc-3019.

kai: Next steps: keep rollout paused. If hotpatch keeps canary stable for 30m, we'll ship targeted selector hotpatch to remaining hosts and follow up with a prefetch tuning PR. If we see any regressions, revert 09b3f and run postmortem.

dev-bot: perf snapshot saved: s3://perf-snapshots/inc-3019/.

oliver: I'll finish the bisect and open a small PR that reverts the selector delta but preserves the prefetch tuning as an experimental flag. Maria and Sophia should validate KV metrics before we re-enable prefetcher.

sophia: A note for long-term: adjust selector cost model to include cold-KV fill penalty; current heuristic only considers kernel throughput without KV cache interaction.

kai: Agreed. Holding thread as canonical for rollout decision and incident notes. Will update when we have stable 30m window or if we revert.
